thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: KV/prefix cache hit-rate collapse detected for tenant AureliaCorp (prod-vpc-us-east-1). Cache miss rate > 95% on prefix 'conv:' across 3 dedicated nodes. Latency spike, 5xx rise. Paging SRE on-call.

pagerduty: Routing page to @maria_chen (sre oncall) — severity P1.

maria_chen: picking this up. seeing 4xx/5xx burst correlated with cache miss-rate. Can someone post the short query that triggered the spike?

alex_gonzalez: I pushed a canary model update earlier to that VPC and primed some long-running prefix keys. Not sure if it's related.

maria_chen: ok, good to know. alex, which model and which prefix?

alex_gonzalez: model: redwood-v2-small-quantized, prefix key: conv:user:* (we were pre-caching conv histories for warm starts).

carmen_sre: Aurelia reports degraded latency for chat endpoints. CS is on a call with Chris at Aurelia. They're seeing 30% errors on long-convo requests.

maria_chen: status checks: hitting dedicated pool dp-us-east-3. cache CPU is normal, memory ~75%. Misses jumped at 13:04 UTC. QPS steady.

leo_kim: looks like prefix collision: our prefetcher primed a huge number of keys with a generic prefix, causing polluting of tenant-local LRU -> thrash. Other tenants on same pool experienced reduced effective cache.

maria_chen: immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) disable prefix prefetching for tenant AureliaCorp, 2) flush Aurelia prefix namespace, 3) enable tenant-isolation mode to pin cache slices (if supported), 4) roll back canary if needed. Thoughts?

alex_gonzalez: agree. I'll disable the prefetch job. Command: ``redwood-scheduler stop job prefetch-aurelia``. Doing it now.

ops-bot: Job prefetch-aurelia stopped (requested by alex_gonzalez).

maria_chen: Carmen, can you ask the customer to pause long-history requests briefly? We want to reduce write pressure while we clean up.

carmen_sre: On the call now — Chris asked for ETA. I'll tell them ~10-15 mins for initial flush and validation.

leo_kim: Preparing namespace flush. Two options: targeted DEL of Aurelia prefixes or a soft TTL bump. DEL may cause a spike as clients repopulate. Recommend TTL bump to 1s for 30s, then revert. Command: ``redwood-cli cache set-ttl --tenant AureliaCorp --prefix conv: --ttl 1 --duration 30``.

maria_chen: good call. Do TTL bump first. Alex, can you confirm the command in the control plane?

alex_gonzalez: running now.

ops-bot: cache TTL update succeeded for tenant AureliaCorp prefix conv: -> ttl=1s for 30s

maria_chen: monitoring. hit-rate trending up?

(30s later)

maria_chen: hit-rate recovered to ~62% from 5% after TTL bump, error rate falling. Latency improving but still above baseline.

leo_kim: Next step: enable tenant cache slice pinning for Aurelia to avoid future pollution. This will isolate their keys to dedicated segments. Command: ``redwood-ops set-cache-isolation --tenant AureliaCorp --mode pinned``. This will require a brief rolling restart of the cache shards on dp-us-east-3 (expected 60s window). Need approval.

carmen_sre: Aurelia on call approves a short maintenance window if it buys stability. Chris confirms.

maria_chen: I approve. Alex, coordinate restart with ops.

alex_gonzalez: scheduling rolling restart now. Will do one shard at a time to keep capacity.

ops-bot: Initiating rolling restart of cache shards (dp-us-east-3) for cache isolation config. Estimated 6 shards, ~12min total.

(rolling restarts proceed)

maria_chen: handoff time in 30m. leo, please take point for the post-mitigation verification and customer follow-up after I sign off.

leo_kim: I'll take it. Checklist: confirm sustained hit-rate >60%, error rate <= baseline+5%, no spillover to other tenants, confirm logs for no new TTL storms.

eng-cs: Chris from Aurelia says they're seeing recovery on their side. Asking for a root cause summary and any client-side mitigations to avoid re-triggering.

maria_chen: root cause (initial): aggressive, unscoped prefetch job primed a large set of conv:* keys without tenant isolation, causing LRU eviction and effective hit-rate collapse for that dedicated pool. Secondary contributor: canary model change changed access patterns and increased prefix cardinality.

maria_chen: actions taken: stopped prefetch job, transient TTL bump to 1s to allow GC of polluted prefixes, enabled tenant cache pinning (isolation), rolled config via rolling restart, coordinated with customer to throttle long-history requests during mitigation.

maria_chen: longer-term next steps: 1) add guardrail to prefetch jobs to respect tenant prefix limits, 2) enforce per-tenant cache quotas in dedicated pools, 3) add preflight check on canary that simulates prefix cardinality, 4) provide customer-facing incident report.

leo_kim: adding an alert rule to detect sudden increase in prefix cardinality per tenant (threshold). I'll put a task in backlog and tag eng-ml for prefetch logic.

carmen_sre: Chris asked for timeline for postmortem and action items. We'll send an interim summary in 2 hours and full postmortem within 48 hours.

maria_chen: handing off to @leo_kim for ongoing monitoring and postmortem. I'm unresponsive for rotation at 21:00 UTC.

leo_kim: taking over. I'll keep the channel updated. Current metrics: hit-rate 78%, 5xxs down to baseline, latency within 10% of baseline.

eng-cs: Thanks all — Aurelia SRE Chris: "app seems stable, thanks for the quick response" :thumbsup:. We'll follow up on customer comms.

ops-bot: Incident status changed to: mitigated (P1 -> monitoring). Incident note appended to incident log.

leo_kim: will open postmortem doc and link here. assigning action owners.

(END of thread)
